Cross-country spillovers from the refined core system (stage 2c)

Demand, monetary and oil shocks on the four-refinement system — and what survives a seed placebo

1. What this is, and what is different from stage 2b

This is the same battery reports/stage2_spillovers.qmd ran, re-run on the stage 2c system: eleven countries, four refinements, k = 76 and df = 22 — identical to stage 2b. That equality is what makes this report worth writing. Every previous extension in this project traded degrees of freedom for structure, so a change in the spillover matrix could always be attributed to a thinner posterior; here it cannot.

Method, unchanged from stage 2b and not re-derived here:

  • koma has no impulse-response function. A shock response is two koma::forecast() calls — one unconditional, one with restrictions = — differenced, with set.seed() immediately before each so the two legs share the identical innovation draw (scenario_diff()).
  • Demand shocks: <iso2>_gdp growth restricted to baseline +1pp at horizon 1 only. A one-quarter growth impulse, not a permanent level step.
  • Monetary shock: ea_policy_rate at baseline +100bp for 4 quarters.
  • Oil shock: oil_price level ×1.5, sustained. Oil is exogenous, so it cannot use restrictions at all — a whole shocked copy of the fit is built instead.
  • Every table is keyed off median_diff, never mean_diff — see §2.
How each exogenous series was extended to reach an 8-quarter horizon. Trailing-momentum continuation, not a forecast of oil markets or world trade.

2. Numerical health of the posterior

2.1 Explosive draws

koma’s Gibbs sampler places no stationarity constraint on a draw’s coefficients, so on a system of this size a real share of posterior draws are dynamically explosive. This is a property of the fitted posterior, not a bug, and it is why every point estimate below is a median.

Averaged over all eleven demand shocks and all eleven GDP variables.
Horizon Mean explosive share across GDP variables
1 0.035
2 0.146
3 0.260
4 0.347
5 0.423
6 0.480
7 0.522
8 0.558

At horizon 8, 549 of 1000 unconditional baseline draws exceed |de_gdp| > 100 — 54.9%, against the 56.8% reports/stage2_spillovers.qmd recorded for stage 2b. Materially the same; stage 2c does not fix the explosive-draw population, and was not expected to.

2.2 Draws the monetary restriction kills outright

A sustained 4-quarter restriction is a different failure mode from an extreme value: restricting four horizons at once requires inverting R %*% Omega %*% t(R), and for a numerically rank-deficient draw no valid conditional innovation exists. koma drops such draws by subsetting the list, recording nothing about which index they were, so scenario_diff() aborts on the draw-count mismatch rather than silently mispair the common random numbers.

failed_restriction_draws() recovers the indices by tracing koma:::forecast_draw() and asking, per draw, whether it returned normally.

Verification before dropping them from the baseline leg.
quantity value
draws attempted 1000
draws failing the conditional solve 40
of those, also explosive in the unconditional baseline 40 of 40
identical failing index set at the placebo seed TRUE

Both checks matter. All 40 failing draws are also explosive — the same badly-behaved population surfacing as an outright failure under a demanding restriction and as a blow-up without one, exactly as stage 2b found (38 of 38 there). And the failing set is identical at both seeds, not merely the same size, which is the prediction the mechanism makes: failure depends on the draw’s posterior Omega, which carries no RNG, while the seed controls only the innovation draw.

5. Common monetary shock

ea_policy_rate +100bp, sustained for 4 quarters, with the 40 singular-solve draws of §2.2 dropped from both legs.

This is the shock stage 2c exists for. Stage 2b’s ea_policy_rate reached 91 of 103 endogenous variables and not one price, so the Taylor rule’s inflation term responded to something nothing it did could influence; stage 2c’s reaches all 114, all 12 prices included. The structural gap is closed and exactly verifiable. The question here is whether the numbers moved.

Three things to read off this, in order of confidence.

The price sign is wrong in both systems, and stage 2c did not fix it. Every one of the eleven price peaks is positive — a tightening appearing to raise prices. §7 shows this is not a broken price block: the same equations respond correctly and substantially to an oil shock. The Phillips-curve link is correctly signed in 10 of 11 countries. What goes wrong is upstream: the policy shock’s effect on GDP is positive at horizon 1 (the simultaneity echo), the price response is almost entirely a horizon-1 effect, and prices are faithfully tracking the wrong part of the GDP path.

The GDP response is still dominated by the horizon-1 echo. Eight of eleven still peak at horizon 1 with a positive value — the same-quarter artefact of imposing an exact-value restriction, diagnosed in stage 2b’s §1.3.

The apparent gain in cumulative GDP sign does not survive the placebo — see §9.1. Greece and Ireland are the exceptions, and the only two countries whose monetary response can honestly be called changed.

8. Sanity checks

All three checks, both systems, reported as-is.
check stage2b stage2c
own effect exceeds every cross-country effect FAIL — 7/11 countries: own > max|cross| PASS — 11/11 countries: own > max|cross|
monetary contraction is negative for GDP and prices everywhere FAIL — GDP peak negative: 2/11 | prices peak negative: 1/11 FAIL — GDP peak negative: 3/11 | prices peak negative: 0/11
spillover magnitude correlates with bilateral trade weight FAIL — Spearman rho = 0.141 (pass threshold: > 0.3) FAIL — Spearman rho = 0.292 (pass threshold: > 0.3)

8.1 Own effect: 7/11 → 11/11, and the Austria artefact is gone

Stage 2b failed this for four countries. A French, German or Belgian demand shock moved Austrian GDP more than it moved the source’s own — an indirect two-hop path through Germany, which §7.1 of that report analysed at length and concluded was a legitimate property of a simultaneous system rather than a defect. Under stage 2c the own effect dominates in 11 of 11.

Austria’s stage-2c foreign_demand weights – now over partner IMPORTS, with row_gdp the unmodelled-world residual.
loads_on weight
be_imports 0.027
de_imports 0.286
es_imports 0.019
fr_imports 0.036
ie_imports 0.016
it_imports 0.056
nl_imports 0.049
us_imports 0.058
row_gdp 0.453

The plausible mechanism is refinement 2. Austria’s exposure is unchanged as a set of trade weights, but what those weights now multiply is partner imports rather than partner GDP. A German demand shock raises German GDP a lot and German imports proportionally less, so the two-hop path into Austria is damped relative to the source’s own response. This report does not claim to have isolated that mechanism — it is the reading consistent with the change, and the alternative explanations (the Phillips curve, the spread) do not touch the demand-propagation path at all.

8.2 Trade-weight correlation: 0.141 → 0.292, still failing

Better by more than a factor of two, and still short of the 0.3 threshold. The structural argument stage 2b’s §7.3 made still applies: this check correlates each cell against the receiver’s direct bilateral weight on the source, in a system where a large share of any country’s total exposure runs through third countries. A network-aware version would be the right test, and remains follow-up work.

This number would not exist at all without a fix made for this stage. spillover_sanity_checks() looked each source up as <source>_gdp in the receiver’s foreign_demand weights. Stage 2c’s identity loads partner imports, so under the old code every lookup missed, the weight column came out all zeros, and the reported correlation was computed against a constant — a meaningless verdict rather than an error. The lookup now matches on the ISO-2 prefix, which also repairs the same latent bug under ireland_proxy.

8.3 Monetary sign: still failing, for a diagnosed reason

Covered in §5.1: the price response is wrong-signed in all eleven countries because the policy rate’s route into GDP is dominated by the horizon-1 simultaneity echo. The check’s premise — that there is a real monetary channel whose sign can be tested — is closer to holding than it was in stage 2b, but it does not yet hold.

9. The seed placebo

Common random numbers make a baseline-vs-scenario pair exact. They do nothing about sampling error in the level of the estimand itself, which is a median over draws of which more than half have exploded by horizon 8. So before any of §5–§8 is read as a stage-2c effect, the same four source countries were re-run at a second seed on the same fit. Anything smaller than that gap is noise.

Four sources (de, fr, it, nl) x 11 receivers = 44 cells.
comparison mean_abs_diff max_abs_diff sign_flips
seed A vs seed B, same stage-2c fit (noise) 0.119 0.356 1
stage 2c vs stage 2b, same seed (the claim) 0.396 1.675 3

Two readings, and the second is the more valuable.

The matrix change is signal. The cross-system difference is 3.3x the seed-to-seed spread, and 26 of 44 cells move by more than twice the noise.

Stage 2c’s matrix is about three times more reproducible than stage 2b’s. CLAUDE.md records stage 2b’s own seed sensitivity: an off-diagonal cell moved by 0.35 on average, up to 1.85, flipping the sign of 7–10 of 30. The same measurement on stage 2c gives 0.119, 0.356, and 1 of 44. That is not a claim that can itself be dismissed as noise — it is a measurement of the noise — and it is the strongest single result in this report. A matrix whose cells were previously too unstable to read individually is now substantially closer to being readable.

Own diagonals. A change is reportable only where the system gap clearly exceeds the seed spread.
country own_2b own_2c_seedA own_2c_seedB seed_spread system_gap

fr 1.658 1.448 1.432 0.016 0.210
it 1.371 1.163 1.129 0.034 0.209
nl 1.008 1.290 1.311 0.021 0.282

France, Italy and the Netherlands move by roughly ten times their seed spread and can be reported. Germany’s diagonal moves by less than its own seed spread (0.103 against 0.183) and must not be. The same discipline that killed the two largest apparent findings in reports/stage3c_rollout.qmd §4.4 applies here and lands on a different country.

The count of countries with a negative cumulative GDP response is 8 at seed A and 6 at seed B — against 6 in stage 2b. The stage-2c “improvement” is smaller than the distance between two runs of stage 2c itself, so it is not a finding. Mean seed gap 0.250 against a mean cross-system gap of 0.409; for 7 of eleven the cross-system gap is smaller than the seed spread.

What survives is Greece (system gap 1.78 against a seed spread of 0.19) and Ireland (1.05 against 0.32), both substantially more contractionary under stage 2c and both among the countries whose response peaks at a later horizon. Portugal clears the same bar only because its seed spread is unusually small (0.030) on a movement of 0.17 in the opposite direction, and is better read as unresolvable than as a third finding. Germany’s gap (0.43) is not clearly above its seed spread (0.37).

10. Verdict

The spillover structure is materially better; the monetary transmission is not. Both halves of that are worth stating precisely, because the second is the one stage 2c was designed to fix.

Better, and it survives the placebo:

  • The own-effect sanity check goes from 7/11 (fail) to 11/11 (pass). Stage 2b’s Austria two-hop artefact — the largest anomaly in that report — is gone.
  • The trade-weight correlation more than doubles (0.141 → 0.292), though it still misses the threshold.
  • The matrix is ~3× more seed-reproducible (mean cell movement 0.119 against 0.35; one sign flip in 44 cells against 7–10 in 30). For a matrix whose cells CLAUDE.md warns must never be read individually, this is the most useful improvement of the three.

Not better:

  • Prices respond to a monetary tightening with the wrong sign in all eleven countries, in both systems.
  • The GDP response still concentrates in a horizon-1 simultaneity echo, and the apparent improvement in its cumulative sign fails the seed placebo. Only Greece and Ireland change by more than noise.
  • The explosive-draw population is unchanged (~55% at horizon 8).

The diagnosis is specific rather than a shrug. Closing the loop structurally was necessary — ea_policy_rate genuinely could not reach a single price variable before, and now reaches all twelve — but the fitted magnitudes along that path are tiny (monetary_loop() gives a contemporaneous round-trip gain around 1e-5, see reports/stage2c_refined_core.qmd §4.5), and 3 of 11 consumption-rate loadings are wrong-signed. The oil shock confirms the price block itself is sound. What is missing is a lagged demand channel from the policy rate strong enough to outweigh the within-quarter restriction artefact — not another contemporaneous link, which is what stage 2c added.
